approved: Supported the tobacco excise bills as building on Labor's plain packaging reforms, noting smoking kills about six million people worldwide and over 15,000 Australians each year, and said the bills would raise the excise share of a cigarette pack's price to 62 per cent by 1 September 2016.

Supported the tobacco excise bills, saying the increases will raise $6.5 billion over the forward estimates, and cited a fall in the national smoking rate to 20 per cent, though Indigenous smoking rates remain around 49 per cent.

Supported the tobacco excise bills, crediting Labor's plain packaging reform with a 78 per cent rise in calls to the Quitline, and highlighted the $14.5 million Indigenous Tobacco Control Initiative that funded projects in 18 Indigenous communities.

Supported the tobacco excise bills, saying smoking costs Australia $31.5 billion a year and kills 15,500 Australians annually, said daily smoking among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people fell from 51 per cent in 2002 to 41 per cent, and called on the National Party to follow Labor, which stopped accepting tobacco donations in 2004, and stop taking donations from tobacco companies.

Supported the tobacco excise bills, noting the 1 December excise increase added $1.23 to a packet of Winfield 25s taking the average price to $19.14, said the measure will deliver a net cash benefit of $370 million in the 2013 to 2014 financial year rising to $2.19 billion by 2016 to 2017, and warned it is a regressive tax that will harm the lowest socioeconomic groups.

Supported the tobacco excise bills, said Australia's smoking rate fell from 25 per cent in 1991 to just under 16 per cent in 2010 against a COAG target of 10 per cent by 2018, cited a 25 per cent excise rise in April 2010 that cut tobacco consumption by about 10.2 per cent, and said heart attack risk drops sharply within a year of quitting while lung cancer death risk halves after 10 years.

Supported the tobacco excise bills, said tobacco is responsible for 7.8 per cent of Australia's total disease burden and 15,551 deaths a year, said alcohol-related harm cost Australia an estimated $14.352 billion in 2010, and called for mandatory alcohol warning labels similar to tobacco's plain packaging regime.

Supported the tobacco excise bills, said tax makes up only 60 per cent of the cigarette price in Australia compared with 74 per cent in New Zealand, 77 per cent in the United Kingdom and 80 per cent in France, cited Treasury findings that the April 2010 25 per cent excise rise cut tobacco consumption by about 11 per cent, and said smoking costs Australia about $31 billion a year including 750,000 hospital bed days.

Supported the tobacco excise bills, said Australia's tobacco excise is only 51 per cent of the retail price against a World Health Organization recommendation of at least 70 per cent, said the Liberal Party has accepted more than $3 million in tobacco donations since 1999, and said the National Party confirmed on 4 February that it was still accepting tobacco industry donations.
